records.literal_gloss: And drew near [the] daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, of [the] clans of Manasseh son of Joseph; and these [are the] names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.

en.L: And the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, drew near; and these [are the] names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
en.B: Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, and belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. His daughters were named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
en.R: Zelophehad had five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. Their family came from the tribe of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, and Hepher was a descendant of Gilead, Machir and Manasseh. One day his daughters came forward with a request.

es.L: Y se acercaron las hijas de Zelofehad hijo de Hefer, hijo de Galaad, hijo de Maquir, hijo de Manasés, de los clanes de Manasés hijo de José; y estos [son los] nombres de sus hijas: Majlá, Noa, y Hoglá, y Milca, y Tirsa.
es.B: Entonces se presentaron las hijas de Zelofehad. Zelofehad era hijo de Hefer, hijo de Galaad, hijo de Maquir, hijo de Manasés, y pertenecía a los clanes de Manasés hijo de José. Sus hijas se llamaban Majlá, Noa, Hoglá, Milca y Tirsa.
es.R: Zelofehad tenía cinco hijas: Majlá, Noa, Hoglá, Milca y Tirsa. Su familia era de la tribu de Manasés, el hijo de José. Zelofehad era hijo de Hefer, y Hefer era descendiente de Galaad, de Maquir y de Manasés. Un día, sus hijas se presentaron para hacer una petición.

fr.L: Et les filles de Tselophehad fils de Hépher, fils de Galaad, fils de Makir, fils de Manassé, des clans de Manassé fils de Joseph, s’approchèrent ; et voici les noms de ses filles : Mahla, Noa, et Hogla, et Milka, et Tirtsa.
fr.B: Alors les filles de Tselophehad s’avancèrent. Tselophehad était fils de Hépher, fils de Galaad, fils de Makir, fils de Manassé, et il appartenait aux clans de Manassé fils de Joseph. Ses filles s’appelaient Mahla, Noa, Hogla, Milka et Tirtsa.
fr.R: Tselophehad avait cinq filles : Mahla, Noa, Hogla, Milka et Tirtsa. Leur famille venait de la tribu de Manassé, le fils de Joseph. Tselophehad était le fils de Hépher, et Hépher était un descendant de Galaad, de Makir et de Manassé. Un jour, ses filles se sont avancées pour présenter une demande.

sw.L: Kisha binti za Selofehadi mwana wa Heferi, mwana wa Gileadi, mwana wa Makiri, mwana wa Manase, wa koo za Manase mwana wa Yusufu, wakakaribia; na haya [ndiyo] majina ya binti zake: Mahla, Noa, na Hogla, na Milka, na Tirsa.
sw.B: Kisha binti za Selofehadi wakaja mbele. Selofehadi alikuwa mwana wa Heferi, mwana wa Gileadi, mwana wa Makiri, mwana wa Manase, naye alikuwa wa koo za Manase mwana wa Yusufu. Binti zake waliitwa Mahla, Noa, Hogla, Milka na Tirsa.
sw.R: Selofehadi alikuwa na binti watano: Mahla, Noa, Hogla, Milka na Tirsa. Jamaa yao ilitoka katika kabila la Manase, mwana wa Yusufu. Selofehadi alikuwa mwana wa Heferi, na Heferi alikuwa mzao wa Gileadi, Makiri na Manase. Siku moja binti zake walikuja mbele wakiwa na ombi.

vi.L: Và các con gái của Xê-lô-phát, con trai Hê-phe, con trai Ga-la-át, con trai Ma-ki, con trai Ma-na-se, thuộc các gia tộc của Ma-na-se con trai Giô-sép, đến gần; và đây [là] tên các con gái ông: Mách-la, Nô-a, Hốt-la, Minh-ca và Thiệt-sa.
vi.B: Bấy giờ các con gái của Xê-lô-phát đến trình diện. Xê-lô-phát là con trai Hê-phe, con trai Ga-la-át, con trai Ma-ki, con trai Ma-na-se, thuộc các gia tộc của Ma-na-se con trai Giô-sép. Các con gái ông tên là Mách-la, Nô-a, Hốt-la, Minh-ca và Thiệt-sa.
vi.R: Xê-lô-phát có năm người con gái: Mách-la, Nô-a, Hốt-la, Minh-ca và Thiệt-sa. Gia đình họ thuộc chi tộc Ma-na-se, con trai Giô-sép. Xê-lô-phát là con trai Hê-phe, còn Hê-phe là con cháu của Ga-la-át, Ma-ki và Ma-na-se. Một ngày kia, các con gái ông đến xin một điều.

ko.L: 그리고 요셉의 아들 므낫세의 가문들에 속한, 므낫세의 아들 마길의 아들 길르앗의 아들 헤벨의 아들 슬로브핫의 딸들이 가까이 나아왔다. 그의 딸들의 이름은 말라, 노아, 호글라, 밀가, 디르사이다.
ko.B: 그때 슬로브핫의 딸들이 앞으로 나아왔다. 슬로브핫은 헤벨의 아들이고, 헤벨은 길르앗의 아들, 길르앗은 마길의 아들, 마길은 므낫세의 아들이었다. 그는 요셉의 아들 므낫세의 가문에 속한 사람이었다. 그의 딸들의 이름은 말라, 노아, 호글라, 밀가, 디르사였다.
ko.R: 슬로브핫에게는 딸이 다섯 있었다. 말라, 노아, 호글라, 밀가, 디르사였다. 그들의 집안은 요셉의 아들 므낫세 지파에 속해 있었다. 슬로브핫은 헤벨의 아들이었고, 헤벨은 길르앗과 마길과 므낫세의 자손이었다. 어느 날 슬로브핫의 딸들이 부탁할 것이 있어서 앞으로 나아왔다.

pt.L: E as filhas de Zelofeade, filho de Hefer, filho de Gileade, filho de Maquir, filho de Manassés, dos clãs de Manassés, filho de José, se aproximaram; e estes [são] os nomes das suas filhas: Maalá, Noa, e Hogla, e Milca, e Tirza.
pt.B: Então as filhas de Zelofeade se apresentaram. Zelofeade era filho de Hefer, filho de Gileade, filho de Maquir, filho de Manassés, e pertencia aos clãs de Manassés, filho de José. As filhas dele se chamavam Maalá, Noa, Hogla, Milca e Tirza.
pt.R: Zelofeade tinha cinco filhas: Maalá, Noa, Hogla, Milca e Tirza. A família delas era da tribo de Manassés, filho de José. Zelofeade era filho de Hefer, e Hefer era descendente de Gileade, de Maquir e de Manassés. Um dia, as filhas de Zelofeade se apresentaram com um pedido.

am.L: ከዮሴፍ ልጅ ከምናሴ ጎሳዎች የሆኑት፣ የምናሴ ልጅ የማኪር ልጅ የገለዓድ ልጅ የሔፌር ልጅ የሰለጰዓድ ሴቶች ልጆች ቀረቡ፤ የሴቶች ልጆቹም ስሞች እነዚህ [ናቸው]፦ ማህላ፣ ኑኃ፣ ዔግላ፣ ሚልካና ቲርጻ።
am.B: ከዚያም የሰለጰዓድ ሴቶች ልጆች ቀረቡ። ሰለጰዓድ የሔፌር ልጅ፣ የገለዓድ ልጅ፣ የማኪር ልጅ፣ የምናሴ ልጅ ሲሆን ከዮሴፍ ልጅ ከምናሴ ጎሳዎች ወገን ነበረ። የሴቶች ልጆቹም ስም ማህላ፣ ኑኃ፣ ዔግላ፣ ሚልካና ቲርጻ ነበረ።
am.R: ሰለጰዓድ ማህላ፣ ኑኃ፣ ዔግላ፣ ሚልካና ቲርጻ የተባሉ አምስት ሴቶች ልጆች ነበሩት። ቤተሰባቸው የዮሴፍ ልጅ ከሆነው ከምናሴ ነገድ ነበረ። ሰለጰዓድ የሔፌር ልጅ ነበረ፤ ሔፌርም የገለዓድ፣ የማኪርና የምናሴ ዘር ነበረ። አንድ ቀን ሴቶች ልጆቹ አንድ ልመና ይዘው ቀረቡ።

decisions.choice: Zelophehad and his daughters: the family named in the census of chapter 26
decisions.reason: The census just taken lists Zelophehad son of Hepher of the clan of Manasseh as a man who had daughters and no sons, and names these five women (26:33). The land was to be shared out by the names counted in that census (26:52-56), so the daughters now ask what will happen to their father's share. Their case returns in 36:1-12 and Joshua 17:3-6.

decisions.choice: drew near: came forward to present a case
decisions.reason: The verb means to come near or approach. Here it is the formal step of coming before the leaders to put a matter to them, as the next verse describes.

decisions.choice: of the clans of Manasseh: their place in the tribe that the land is shared by
decisions.reason: The family line is traced back six generations to Joseph. Land in Israel was held by tribe, clan and family, so a person's line decided where his share of the land would be.

decisions.choice: names first, then the family line
decisions.reason: Readable gives the five names first and the long family line after it in short sentences, so young readers can follow who is meant. It adds "with a request" to lead into verses 2-4, which say what they asked.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("s'approchèrent", "s'avancèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("se sont avancées")
decisions.reason: Narrative tenses follow docs/french-style.md section 3, as in the rest of Numbers.

decisions.choice: Names in their usual Protestant Korean forms: "슬로브핫", "헤벨", "마길", and the daughters "말라", "노아", "호글라", "밀가", "디르사"
decisions.reason: "슬로브핫" and "마길" are the forms already used in Korean 1 Chronicles 7:15, "디르사" the form of the town in Korean 1 Kings; the names stay the same in Numbers 36 and Joshua 17.

decisions.choice: The line of descent runs from Manasseh down to Zelophehad ("므낫세의 아들 마길의 아들 ... 헤벨의 아들 슬로브핫")
decisions.reason: A Korean noun phrase puts its modifiers before the noun, so the chain of "son of" that follows the name in Hebrew comes before it in Korean; Balanced and Readable break it into short sentences.

decisions.choice: The names as in Joshua 17:3 and 1 Chronicles 7: "Xê-lô-phát", "Mách-la", "Nô-a", "Hốt-la", "Minh-ca", "Thiệt-sa"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms already used in the Vietnamese Joshua, kept for the same family.

decisions.choice: "đến trình diện" (B); "đến xin một điều" (R)
decisions.reason: The daughters come forward to present a case; plain "đến gần" (kept at L) would only say they moved closer.

decisions.choice: se aproximaram (L); se apresentaram (B, R); Zelofeade, Maalá, Noa, Hogla, Milca, Tirza
decisions.reason: The verb is the formal step of coming before the leaders with a case (m2): Literal keeps "se aproximaram", and Balanced and Readable say "se apresentaram", the Portuguese for presenting oneself before an authority. The names are those set at 26:33, "Noa" kept apart from "Noé".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalizes pronouns for God (verses 14 and 21 in English) has nothing to change; the Amharic text of this chapter has no such spans.

source.text: וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֜דְנָה לִפְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֗ה וְלִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הַנְּשִׂיאִ֖ם וְכָל־הָעֵדָ֑ה פֶּ֥תַח אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר׃

am.R: በመገናኛው ድንኳን በር ላይ በሙሴ፣ በካህኑ በአልዓዛር፣ በመሪዎቹና በማኅበሩ ሁሉ ፊት ቆሙ። እንዲህም አሉ፦

decisions.choice: at the entrance of the tent of meeting: the place where public cases were heard before the LORD
decisions.reason: The open space before the entrance of the tent was where the people gathered before the LORD and where matters too hard for the people were brought (Leviticus 8:3-4; Numbers 16:18-19). Bringing their case there put it before Moses, the priest and the people, and before the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: Eleazar the priest: Aaron's son, now high priest
decisions.reason: Aaron had died and Eleazar had taken his place (20:25-28). He stands beside Moses here as he did at the census (26:1, 63).

decisions.choice: The daughters speak to Moses and the leaders in 합쇼체 with "우리" (verses 3-4)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet sets for the people speaking to Moses; they bring a case before the leaders of the whole congregation.

decisions.choice: "các thủ lĩnh" for the leaders (nesi'im) of the congregation
decisions.reason: A plain modern word for the tribal leaders; used through this batch.

source.text: אָבִינוּ֮ מֵ֣ת בַּמִּדְבָּר֒ וְה֨וּא לֹא־הָיָ֜ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעֵדָ֗ה הַנּוֹעָדִ֛ים עַל־יְהוָ֖ה בַּעֲדַת־קֹ֑רַח כִּֽי־בְחֶטְא֣וֹ מֵ֔ת וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־הָ֥יוּ לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in [the] midst of the company, the [ones] gathered together against Yahweh in [the] company of Korah; for in his own sin he died, and sons there were not to him.

en.L: "Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the company that gathered together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the company of Korah; for he died in his own sin, and he had no sons.
en.B: "Our father died in the wilderness. He was not one of the company who banded together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the company of Korah. He died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
en.R: "Our father died in the desert. He was not one of Korah's followers, who joined together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.

es.L: «Nuestro padre murió en el desierto, y él no estaba en medio del grupo de los que se juntaron contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} en el grupo de Coré; porque en su propio pecado murió, y no tuvo hijos [varones].
es.B: «Nuestro padre murió en el desierto. No fue de los del grupo que se confabuló contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el grupo de Coré. Murió por su propio pecado, y no tuvo hijos varones.
es.R: «Nuestro padre murió en el desierto. No era uno de los seguidores de Coré, que se unieron contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Murió a causa de su propio pecado, y no tuvo hijos varones.

fr.L: « Notre père est mort dans le désert, et il n’était pas au milieu de la bande qui s’était liguée contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dans la bande de Coré ; car il est mort dans son propre péché, et il n’avait pas de fils.
fr.B: « Notre père est mort dans le désert. Il ne faisait pas partie de la bande qui s’était liguée contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, la bande de Coré. Il est mort pour son propre péché, et il n’avait pas de fils.
fr.R: « Notre père est mort dans le désert. Il n’était pas un des partisans de Coré, qui s’étaient unis contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Il est mort à cause de son propre péché, et il n’avait pas de fils.

sw.L: "Baba yetu alikufa nyikani, wala yeye hakuwa miongoni mwa kundi lile lililokusanyika pamoja dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika kundi la Kora; kwa maana alikufa katika dhambi yake mwenyewe, wala hakuwa na wana [wa kiume].
sw.B: "Baba yetu alikufa nyikani. Hakuwa mmoja wa kundi lile lililoungana dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kundi la Kora. Alikufa kwa ajili ya dhambi yake mwenyewe, wala hakuwa na wana wa kiume.
sw.R: "Baba yetu alikufa jangwani. Hakuwa mmoja wa wafuasi wa Kora, walioungana dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Alikufa kwa sababu ya dhambi yake mwenyewe, wala hakuwa na wana wa kiume.

vi.L: "Cha chúng tôi đã chết trong hoang mạc, và ông không ở giữa bọn người đã họp nhau chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trong bè đảng của Cô-rê; vì ông đã chết trong tội của chính mình, và ông không có con trai.
vi.B: "Cha chúng tôi đã chết trong hoang mạc. Ông không thuộc bè đảng đã kéo nhau chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, là bè đảng của Cô-rê. Ông chết vì tội riêng của mình, và ông không có con trai.
vi.R: "Cha chúng tôi đã chết trong hoang mạc. Ông không theo phe Cô-rê, là những người đã hiệp nhau chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ông chết vì tội của chính ông, và ông không có con trai.

ko.L: "우리 아버지는 광야에서 죽었습니다. 그러나 그는 고라의 무리 가운데서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 함께 모였던 무리 가운데 있지 않았습니다. 그는 자기 죄로 죽었고, 그에게는 아들들이 없었습니다.
ko.B: "우리 아버지는 광야에서 죽었습니다. 그러나 아버지는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 거슬러 모인 무리, 곧 고라의 무리에 끼지 않았습니다. 아버지는 자기 죄 때문에 죽었고, 아들이 없었습니다.
ko.R: "우리 아버지는 광야에서 돌아가셨습니다. 아버지는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 맞서려고 모였던 고라의 무리에 끼지 않았습니다. 아버지는 자기 죄 때문에 돌아가셨는데, 아들이 없었습니다.

pt.L: "O nosso pai morreu no deserto, e ele não estava no meio do grupo dos que se juntaram contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} no grupo de Corá; porque ele morreu no seu próprio pecado, e não teve filhos.
pt.B: "O nosso pai morreu no deserto. Ele não fazia parte do grupo dos que se uniram contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o grupo de Corá. Ele morreu pelo seu próprio pecado, e não teve filhos homens.
pt.R: "O nosso pai morreu no deserto. Ele não era um dos seguidores de Corá, que se juntaram contra {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Ele morreu por causa do seu próprio pecado e não teve nenhum filho homem.

am.L: «አባታችን በምድረ በዳ ሞተ፤ እርሱም {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ላይ በቆሬ ወገን ውስጥ ከተሰበሰቡት ወገን መካከል አልነበረም፤ በገዛ ኃጢአቱ ሞቷልና፤ ወንዶች ልጆችም አልነበሩትም።

am.R: «አባታችን በምድረ በዳ ሞተ። እርሱ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ላይ ከተባበሩት ከቆሬ ተከታዮች አንዱ አልነበረም። የሞተው በራሱ ኃጢአት ምክንያት ነው፤ ወንዶች ልጆችም አልነበሩትም።

decisions.choice: not in the company of Korah: their father did not die as one of the rebels
decisions.reason: Korah and his company rose against Moses and Aaron and so against the LORD, and they died under judgment (16:1-35; 26:9-11). The daughters make plain that their father was not one of them. A rebel's family line might be thought to lose its claim, so this answers an objection before it is raised.

decisions.choice: he died in his own sin: he died for his own failings, like the rest of his generation
alternatives: he died for some sin of his own that is not named
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means that he died for his own sins as any person does, sharing the fate of the generation that refused to enter the land and so died in the wilderness (14:29-35; 26:64-65). His death was no special punishment that should cut off his family. It is not a confession of some crime.

decisions.choice: company: Korah's band, with the word used for the congregation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the whole congregation of Israel. Used of Korah's followers, it marks them as a rival congregation (16:5).

decisions.choice: company / followers
decisions.reason: As in 16:5, Literal and Balanced say "company" for Korah's group, keeping "congregation" for Israel as a whole; Readable says "followers".

decisions.choice: hijos [varones] (L); hijos varones (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" can include daughters, and the speakers are his daughters; "varones" makes clear that sons are meant. Literal brackets the added word.

decisions.choice: wana [wa kiume] (L); wana wa kiume (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Wana" alone can mean children of either sex; "wa kiume" makes clear that he had no sons, though he had daughters. Literal brackets the added words.

decisions.choice: "돌아가셨습니다" at Readable for the father's death; "죽었습니다" at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: A daughter speaking of her own father before others would naturally use the honorific verb; Literal and Balanced keep the plain verb of the Hebrew, as the Korean narrative does elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "bè đảng" for Korah's company
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the word for the congregation; Vietnamese "hội chúng" would make Korah's band sound like the whole people, so a word for a faction is used.

decisions.choice: o grupo de Corá (L, B); os seguidores de Corá (R)
decisions.reason: As at 26:9: Korah's band is "o grupo" at Literal and Balanced, so that "comunidade" stays the word for Israel as a whole (m3), and "os seguidores" at Readable. Balanced and Readable say "filhos homens" for "sons", as at 26:33, since Portuguese "filhos" could include the daughters who are speaking.

decisions.choice: "የቆሬ ወገን" (L, B), "የቆሬ ተከታዮች" (R) for Korah's company, as in 26:9
decisions.reason: "ማኅበር" is kept for the congregation of Israel, which the daughters address in the same scene (verse 2).

records.literal_gloss: Why should be taken away [the] name of our father from [the] midst of his clan, because there is not to him a son? Give to us a possession in [the] midst of [the] brothers of our father.

en.L: Why should the name of our father be taken away from the midst of his clan because he had no son? Give us a possession among the brothers of our father."
en.B: Why should our father's name disappear from his clan because he had no son? Give us property among our father's brothers."
en.R: He had no son, but why should that mean our father's name is lost from his clan? Give us land of our own among our father's relatives."

ko.R: 아버지에게 아들이 없다고 해서 아버지의 이름이 가문에서 사라져야 합니까? 우리에게도 아버지의 친척들 사이에서 우리 몫의 땅을 주십시오."

pt.L: Por que o nome do nosso pai seria tirado do meio do seu clã, porque ele não teve filho? Dê-nos uma propriedade no meio dos irmãos do nosso pai."
pt.B: Por que o nome do nosso pai deveria desaparecer do seu clã só porque ele não teve filho homem? Dê-nos uma propriedade entre os irmãos do nosso pai."
pt.R: Ele não teve filho homem, mas por que isso faria o nome do nosso pai desaparecer do seu clã? Dê-nos uma terra que seja nossa, entre os parentes do nosso pai."

am.L: ወንድ ልጅ ስለሌለው የአባታችን ስም ከጎሳው መካከል ለምን ይጥፋ? በአባታችን ወንድሞች መካከል ይዞታ ስጡን።»

decisions.choice: the name taken away: the father's family line and its land would vanish
decisions.reason: A man's "name" lived on in his descendants and in the land that carried his name in the clan's holdings. If no one inherited his share, his line would be forgotten. The same concern lies behind the law of a brother's widow (Deuteronomy 25:6) and Boaz's words in Ruth 4:10.

decisions.choice: a possession: land held as one's own by the family
decisions.reason: The word names land held by a person or family as a lasting property (Genesis 23:4, 20; Leviticus 25:10). The daughters ask for their father's share of the land to be given to them.

decisions.choice: the brothers of our father: their father's male relatives in the clan
decisions.reason: Land was shared out among the men of each clan by their fathers' houses. The daughters ask to stand among their uncles as holders of land, in their father's place.

decisions.choice: property / land of our own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the possession is; Literal keeps "possession".

decisions.choice: "소유지" (Literal) for the possession; "땅" (Balanced), "우리 몫의 땅" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is land held by a family as its own (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say plainly that it is land.

decisions.choice: "Xin cho chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: The daughters ask Moses and the leaders; Vietnamese turns the imperative into a polite request.

decisions.choice: Dê-nos (the "o senhor" form, to Moses)
decisions.reason: The command is singular in the Hebrew, addressed to Moses, the leader before whom the daughters stand. People speak to a superior with "o senhor" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), so the imperative is the third-person "Dê-nos"; "tu" is kept for God. Literal says "propriedade" for the possession (m2), as Balanced does where the English says "property"; Readable says "terra", as the English Readable says "land".

decisions.choice: brought their case before the LORD: asked the LORD for a ruling
decisions.reason: The word for "case" is the word for a judgment or legal ruling. When Moses met a matter the law did not yet cover, he took it to the LORD for a decision, as with the man who cursed the Name (Leviticus 24:12), those unclean at Passover (9:8) and the Sabbath breaker (15:34).

decisions.choice: "사정" for their case
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is the word for a legal case or ruling (meaning decision); "사정" is a matter brought for decision, and "아뢰었다" keeps the respect due to God at Balanced.

records.literal_gloss: Right [the] daughters of Zelophehad [are] speaking. Surely you shall give to them a possession of inheritance in [the] midst of [the] brothers of their father, and you shall make pass over [the] inheritance of their father to them.

en.L: "The daughters of Zelophehad are speaking right. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among the brothers of their father, and you shall make the inheritance of their father pass over to them.
en.B: "The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say. You must give them a property as an inheritance among their father's brothers, and transfer their father's inheritance to them.
en.R: "What the daughters of Zelophehad say is right. You must give them land to own among their father's relatives. Give them the land that would have gone to their father.

decisions.choice: right: their claim is just
decisions.reason: The word means right, true or fitting. The LORD declares that the daughters' claim is justified; the same verdict is given in 36:5 on the claim of their clan.

decisions.choice: surely you shall give: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb "give" to make the command firm and certain.

decisions.choice: a possession of inheritance: land held by right of inheritance
decisions.reason: The two words together name land received as a family's lasting share. The inheritance is the share of the land each family was to receive by lot (26:52-56).

decisions.choice: to them, their father: the first pronouns are masculine, the later ones feminine
decisions.reason: In the first half of the verse the pronouns "them" and "their" have masculine forms, in the second half feminine ones. Hebrew sometimes uses masculine forms for a group of women, and every one of these pronouns refers to the daughters. The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: make pass over: transfer the inheritance to a new holder
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause something to pass from one to another. The father's share is not lost; it passes on to his daughters.

decisions.choice: transfer / give them the land
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "make pass over"; Balanced says "transfer" and Readable gives the sense in plain words.

decisions.choice: "유산" for the inheritance (nachalah) and "넘겨주다" for "make pass over"
decisions.reason: "유산" is the word Korean Joshua uses for the land each family receives (Joshua 13:32); "넘겨주다" says the inheritance passes to a new holder (meaning decision). God speaks to Moses in 해라체 with "너", as everywhere in these books.

decisions.choice: God calls Moses "ngươi" at L and "con" at B and R
decisions.reason: As in Genesis and Exodus: "ngươi" keeps the bare Hebrew "you" at Literal; "con" gives the close, fatherly relation that modern Vietnamese hears in God speaking to his servant.

decisions.choice: "sản nghiệp" for the inheritance (nahalah); "đất sở hữu" (L) / "phần đất" (B) for the possession (ahuzzah)
decisions.reason: "Sản nghiệp" is the land a family holds by right from God, as in Joshua; "gia tài" sounds like movable wealth.

decisions.choice: uma propriedade de herança (L), uma propriedade como herança (B); farás passar a herança (L); transferir o direito de herança (B); Dá a elas a terra (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "o direito de herança" names what passes to the daughters (m3, m5), the right to the family's share of land, as Portuguese law speaks of it; Balanced says "transferir o direito de herança", where Literal keeps the Hebrew picture "fazer passar a herança" and Readable says plainly what they receive, as the English does. The doubled verb (m2) is "certamente" at Literal and "deves" at Balanced and Readable. The LORD speaks to Moses with "tu".

decisions.choice: a law for all Israel from one family's case
decisions.reason: The LORD answers the daughters' case and then makes it a general rule. Verses 8-11 set the order of heirs when a man dies: sons first, as was already the custom, then daughters, then brothers, then his father's brothers, then the nearest relative in the clan.

decisions.choice: a man: the head of a family who holds its land
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a man because land was held in the name of the male head of a family. The point of the law is that his share should pass on and stay within his clan; chapter 36 adds that daughters who inherit are to marry within their father's tribe (36:6-9).

decisions.choice: transfer / give his land
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (Literal), "이스라엘 백성" (Balanced), "이스라엘 사람들" (Readable) for "the sons of Israel", with no gender span; laws in 해라체 (-하라 at Literal and Balanced, -해야 한다 at Readable)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet sets. The Korean words already include women and men, so the gender setting has nothing to change. Recorded once for Numbers 27-33.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L), "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting span, as in the English
decisions.reason: Neither Vietnamese phrase says "sons", so there is nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: The law to the people uses "các ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: God's commands to the people keep "các ngươi", as in Leviticus.

decisions.choice: tu (falarás, diz) to Moses; vocês (farão passar, transferirão, deem) in the law
decisions.reason: The LORD tells Moses (singular) to speak, and the law he gives Israel is in the plural in the Hebrew ("you shall make pass"), so Portuguese turns from "tu" to "vocês" inside the quotation, through verse 11. Balanced and Readable say "filho homem", as at 26:33.

decisions.choice: "የእስራኤል ልጆች" (L, B) and "እስራኤላውያን" (R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: "ልጆች" already includes daughters, so Amharic has no second wording for the English gender spans on "the sons of Israel"; this holds through the chapter. The law itself is addressed to Israel in the plural, so Amharic changes from "አንተ" (Moses) to "እናንተ" here, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: his relative, the nearest to him: his closest kin by blood
decisions.reason: The word for "relative" means one's own flesh, a blood relation (Leviticus 18:6; 25:49). The nearest kinsman of the clan inherits, so the land never leaves the clan.

decisions.choice: a statute of judgment: a fixed rule of law
decisions.reason: "Statute" is a fixed, lasting law and "judgment" a legal ruling. Together they mark this as a standing rule of law for Israel, to be followed in deciding such cases. The phrase is used again in 35:29.

decisions.choice: as the LORD commanded Moses: the narrator's closing words, after the LORD's speech ends
decisions.reason: The LORD's words end with the statute. The last clause is the narrator's formula, telling the reader that this law came from the LORD through Moses. It could also be read as the last words of the speech, but it is the narrator's usual way of closing a law given through Moses (compare verse 22 and 31:31). The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: a statute of judgment / a legal statute / a law
decisions.reason: Literal keeps both words; Balanced joins them as "a legal statute", and Readable says "a law".

decisions.choice: "판결의 규례" (Literal), "법의 규례" (Balanced), "법" (Readable) for "a statute of judgment"
decisions.reason: "규례" is the term sheet word for a statute; "판결" keeps the Hebrew word for judgment at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say that it is a fixed rule of law (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "luật lệ xét xử"
decisions.reason: "Statute" is "luật lệ" and "judgment" (mishpat) "mạng lệnh" on the term sheet; here the pair means one fixed rule of law, so Literal keeps the two words as one phrase.

decisions.choice: um estatuto de juízo (L); um estatuto legal (B); uma lei (R)
decisions.reason: The two words name a fixed rule of law for deciding such cases (m2). Literal keeps both, "estatuto" as the book's word for a statute and "juízo" for a legal ruling; Balanced joins them as "estatuto legal", and Readable says "uma lei", as the English does. The closing words are the narrator's (m3), outside the quotation.

ko.B: 그 뒤에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "아바림 산줄기에 있는 이 산에 올라가서, 내가 이스라엘 백성에게 준 땅을 바라보아라.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "아바림 산지에 있는 이 산 위로 올라가거라. 그리고 내가 이스라엘 사람들에게 준 땅을 내려다보아라.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Sobe a este monte de Abarim e vê a terra que dei aos filhos de Israel.
pt.B: Depois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Sobe este monte na serra de Abarim e contempla a terra que dei aos israelitas.
pt.R: Depois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Sobe neste monte, nos montes de Abarim. Olha a terra que dei aos israelitas.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ሙሴን አለው፦ «ወደዚህ ወደ ዓባሪም ተራራ ውጣ፤ ለእስራኤልም ልጆች የሰጠኋትን ምድር እይ።
am.B: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሙሴን እንዲህ አለው፦ «በዓባሪም ተራሮች ወዳለው ወደዚህ ተራራ ውጣ፤ ለእስራኤል ልጆች የሰጠኋትንም ምድር ተመልከት።
am.R: ከዚያም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሙሴን እንዲህ አለው፦ «በዓባሪም ኮረብቶች ወዳለው ወደዚህ ተራራ ውጣ። ለእስራኤላውያን የሰጠኋትን ምድር ከዚያ ሆነህ ተመልከት።

decisions.choice: the mountain of the Abarim: the heights east of the Jordan facing the land
decisions.reason: The name means "the regions across", the hills on the eastern side of the Dead Sea and the Jordan, opposite Jericho, where Israel was camped (22:1; 33:47-48). Deuteronomy 32:49 and 34:1 name the peak Moses climbed as Mount Nebo in this range.

decisions.choice: I have given: the gift is already settled
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks of the land as already given, though Israel has not yet entered it. The gift is certain because he has decided it (20:12).

decisions.choice: see the land: Moses may see it but not enter it
decisions.reason: Moses is allowed to see the land from far off, as the next verses explain, because he will not go into it (20:12; Deuteronomy 3:23-27; 34:1-4).

decisions.choice: this mountain in the Abarim range / hills
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "range" or "hills" to show that Abarim names a line of heights, not one mountain.

decisions.choice: cette montagne des Abarim (L); la chaîne des Abarim (B); les monts Abarim (R)
decisions.reason: Abarim is a plural name ("the regions across") for a range of heights, so French keeps the plural article "des" with it, as it does with other range names, rather than making it the name of one mountain.

decisions.choice: "아바림 산" (Literal), "아바림 산줄기에 있는 이 산" (Balanced), "아바림 산지" (Readable)
decisions.reason: "아바림" is the usual Protestant form; Abarim is a range of heights east of the Jordan (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable name the range and the one mountain in it.

decisions.choice: na serra de Abarim (B); nos montes de Abarim (R)
decisions.reason: Abarim names a line of heights, not one mountain (m1); Balanced says "serra", the Brazilian word for a range of hills, and Readable "montes", as the English says "range" and "hills".

source.text: וְרָאִ֣יתָה אֹתָ֔הּ וְנֶאֱסַפְתָּ֥ אֶל־עַמֶּ֖יךָ גַּם־אָ֑תָּה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶאֱסַ֖ף אַהֲרֹ֥ן אָחִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will see it, and you will be gathered to your people, also you, as was gathered Aaron your brother,

en.L: And you shall see it, and you shall be gathered to your people, you also, just as Aaron your brother was gathered,
en.B: When you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was,
en.R: After you have seen it, you will die and join your people who died before you, just as your brother Aaron did.

es.L: Y la verás, y serás reunido con tus pueblos, también tú, como fue reunido Aarón tu hermano,
es.B: Cuando la hayas visto, también tú serás reunido con tu pueblo, como lo fue tu hermano Aarón,
es.R: Después de verla, morirás y te unirás a los tuyos que murieron antes que tú, igual que tu hermano Aarón.

fr.L: Et tu le verras, et tu seras réuni à tes peuples, toi aussi, comme Aaron ton frère a été réuni,
fr.B: Quand tu l’auras vu, tu seras toi aussi réuni à ton peuple, comme l’a été ton frère Aaron,
fr.R: Après l’avoir vu, tu mourras et tu rejoindras les tiens qui sont morts avant toi, comme ton frère Aaron.

sw.L: Nawe utaiona, nawe utakusanywa kwa watu wako, wewe pia, kama Haruni ndugu yako alivyokusanywa,
sw.B: Ukisha kuiona, wewe pia utakusanywa pamoja na watu wako, kama ndugu yako Haruni alivyokusanywa,
sw.R: Baada ya kuiona, utakufa na kujiunga na watu wako waliokufa kabla yako, kama ndugu yako Haruni alivyofanya.

vi.L: Và ngươi sẽ thấy nó, và ngươi cũng sẽ được thu về với dân của ngươi, như A-rôn anh ngươi đã được thu về,
vi.B: Sau khi đã thấy xứ ấy, con cũng sẽ được về với tổ tiên như A-rôn anh con,
vi.R: Sau khi con đã thấy xứ ấy, con sẽ qua đời và về với những người trong dân con đã qua đời trước con, như A-rôn anh con vậy.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 그것을 볼 것이고, 네 형 아론이 [그의 백성에게] 모여 간 것처럼 너도 네 백성에게로 모여 갈 것이다.
ko.B: 너는 그 땅을 본 뒤에, 네 형 아론처럼 너도 조상들에게로 돌아갈 것이다.
ko.R: 너는 그 땅을 본 다음에 죽을 것이다. 그리고 네 형 아론처럼 먼저 죽은 네 조상들 곁으로 갈 것이다.

pt.L: E tu a verás, e serás reunido ao teu povo, também tu, como foi reunido Arão, o teu irmão,
pt.B: Depois de vê-la, tu também serás reunido ao teu povo, como foi o teu irmão Arão,
pt.R: Depois de ver a terra, tu vais morrer e te juntar ao teu povo que morreu antes de ti, como aconteceu com o teu irmão Arão.

am.L: ታያታለህ፤ ወንድምህ አሮን እንደ ተሰበሰበ አንተ ደግሞ ወደ ወገኖችህ ትሰበሰባለህ፤
am.B: ካየሃትም በኋላ ወንድምህ አሮን እንደ ተሰበሰበ አንተም ደግሞ ወደ ወገኖችህ ትሰበሰባለህ፤
am.R: ካየሃት በኋላ ትሞታለህ፤ ወንድምህ አሮን እንዳደረገው አንተም ከአንተ በፊት ወደ ሞቱት ወገኖችህ ትሄዳለህ።

decisions.choice: be gathered to your people: die and join one's ancestors
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the death of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Aaron (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; 49:33; Numbers 20:24, 26). It speaks of death as going to be with those of one's family who died before.

decisions.choice: as Aaron your brother was gathered: Aaron's death on Mount Hor
decisions.reason: Aaron had gone up Mount Hor and died there, after his priestly clothes were put on Eleazar (20:22-29). Moses is told that his own death will come in the same way, on a mountain, and that a successor must be named.

decisions.choice: you will die and join your people who died before you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of being gathered to one's people means. Literal and Balanced keep the picture.

decisions.choice: "네 백성에게로 모여 가다" (Literal), "조상들에게로 돌아가다" (Balanced); Readable says "죽을 것이다" plainly
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom means to die and join one's ancestors (meaning decision). Literal keeps its words; Balanced uses the Korean way of speaking of a death as a return to one's forebears; Readable states the death, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "được về với tổ tiên"
decisions.reason: The idiom for dying in peace that the Vietnamese Kings already uses; Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.

decisions.choice: serás reunido ao teu povo (L, B)
decisions.reason: The idiom for death as joining one's family who died before (m1) keeps the wording Genesis 25:8 and 35:29 use in Portuguese, "foi reunido ao seu povo"; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ מְרִיתֶ֨ם פִּ֜י בְּמִדְבַּר־צִ֗ן בִּמְרִיבַת֙ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה לְהַקְדִּישֵׁ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם לְעֵינֵיהֶ֑ם הֵ֛ם מֵֽי־מְרִיבַ֥ת קָדֵ֖שׁ מִדְבַּר־צִֽן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: because you rebelled [against] my mouth in [the] wilderness of Zin, in [the] quarreling of the congregation, to treat as holy me at the waters before their eyes. They [are the] waters of Meribah [of] Kadesh, [in the] wilderness of Zin.

en.L: because you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth in the wilderness of Zin, in the quarreling of the congregation, to treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy at the waters before their eyes." (These [are the] waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)
en.B: for when the congregation quarreled in the wilderness of Zin, you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command to show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness before their eyes at the waters." (These were the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.)
en.R: This is because you and Aaron went against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command in the Zin Desert. When the people quarreled there, you did not show them that I am holy at the water." (This was at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the Zin Desert.)

es.L: porque {{plural_you:se rebelaron|os rebelasteis}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca en el desierto de Zin, en la contienda de la comunidad, para tratarme como santo junto a las aguas a los ojos de ellos». (Estas [son] las aguas de Meribá de Cades, en el desierto de Zin.)
es.B: pues cuando la comunidad se peleó en el desierto de Zin, {{plural_you:ustedes se rebelaron|vosotros os rebelasteis}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mandato de mostrar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} santidad ante sus ojos junto a las aguas». (Estas eran las aguas de Meribá, en Cades, en el desierto de Zin.)
es.R: Esto es porque tú y Aarón {{plural_you:desobedecieron|desobedecisteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} orden en el desierto de Zin. Cuando el pueblo discutió allí, no le {{plural_you:mostraron|mostrasteis}} junto al agua que yo soy santo». (Fue en las aguas de Meribá, en Cades, en el desierto de Zin.)

fr.L: parce que vous vous êtes rebellés contre {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche dans le désert de Tsin, lors de la querelle de la communauté, pour {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} traiter comme saint près des eaux, sous leurs yeux. » (Ce [sont] les eaux de Meriba de Kadesh, dans le désert de Tsin.)
fr.B: car, lorsque la communauté s’est querellée dans le désert de Tsin, vous vous êtes rebellés contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} ordre, qui devait manifester {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sainteté sous leurs yeux, près des eaux. » (C’étaient les eaux de Meriba, à Kadesh, dans le désert de Tsin.)
fr.R: C’est parce que toi et Aaron, vous avez désobéi à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} ordre dans le désert de Tsin. Quand le peuple s’est disputé là-bas, vous ne lui avez pas montré près de l’eau que je suis saint. » (C’était aux eaux de Meriba, à Kadesh, dans le désert de Tsin.)

sw.L: kwa sababu mliasi dhidi ya kinywa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} katika nyika ya Zini, katika ugomvi wa jumuiya, ili kunitakasa kwenye maji mbele ya macho yao." (Hayo [ndiyo] maji ya Meriba ya Kadeshi katika nyika ya Zini.)
sw.B: kwa maana jumuiya ilipogombana katika nyika ya Zini, mliasi dhidi ya agizo {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la kuonyesha utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mbele ya macho yao kwenye maji." (Hayo yalikuwa maji ya Meriba huko Kadeshi, katika nyika ya Zini.)
sw.R: Hii ni kwa sababu wewe na Haruni mlikwenda kinyume na agizo {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} katika jangwa la Zini. Watu walipogombana huko, hamkuwaonyesha kwenye maji kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni mtakatifu." (Hii ilikuwa kwenye maji ya Meriba huko Kadeshi, katika jangwa la Zini.)

vi.L: vì các ngươi đã chống lại miệng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong hoang mạc Xin, khi hội chúng cãi vã, [đáng lẽ phải] tôn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thánh tại dòng nước trước mắt chúng." (Đó [là] dòng nước Mê-ri-ba tại Ca-đe trong hoang mạc Xin.)
vi.B: vì khi hội chúng cãi vã trong hoang mạc Xin, các con đã chống lại lệnh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, không bày tỏ sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước mắt họ tại dòng nước ấy." (Đó là dòng nước Mê-ri-ba tại Ca-đe, trong hoang mạc Xin.)
vi.R: Đó là vì con và A-rôn đã làm trái lệnh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong hoang mạc Xin. Khi dân chúng cãi vã ở đó, các con đã không cho họ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thánh tại dòng nước." (Đó là dòng nước Mê-ri-ba tại Ca-đe, trong hoang mạc Xin.)

ko.L: 너희가 신 광야에서 회중이 다툴 때, 그 물가에서 그들의 눈앞에서 나를 거룩하게 하라는 내 입을 거역하였기 때문이다." (그것은 신 광야 가데스의 므리바 물이다.)
ko.B: 회중이 신 광야에서 다툴 때, 너희는 그 물가에서 그들이 보는 앞에서 나의 거룩함을 드러내라는 내 명령을 거역했다." (그 물은 신 광야 가데스에 있는 므리바 물이다.)
ko.R: 그것은 너와 아론이 신 광야에서 내 명령을 따르지 않았기 때문이다. 백성이 그곳에서 다툴 때, 너희는 물가에서 내가 거룩하다는 것을 그들에게 보여 주지 않았다." (그곳은 신 광야 가데스에 있는 므리바 물이다.)

pt.L: porque vocês se rebelaram contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} boca no deserto de Zim, na contenda da comunidade, para {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} santificar junto às águas diante dos olhos deles." (Estas [são] as águas de Meribá de Cades, no deserto de Zim.)
pt.B: pois, quando a comunidade discutiu no deserto de Zim, vocês se rebelaram contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ordem de mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} santidade diante dos olhos deles, junto às águas." (Essas foram as águas de Meribá, em Cades, no deserto de Zim.)
pt.R: Isso vai acontecer porque tu e Arão desobedeceram à {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ordem no deserto de Zim. Quando o povo discutiu ali, vocês não mostraram a eles que eu sou santo, junto à água." (Isso aconteceu nas águas de Meribá, em Cades, no deserto de Zim.)

am.L: በጺን ምድረ በዳ፣ በማኅበሩ ክርክር ጊዜ፣ በውኃው አጠገብ በዓይናቸው ፊት እኔን [ከመቀደስ ይልቅ] በአፌ ላይ ዐምፃችኋልና።» (እነዚህ በጺን ምድረ በዳ ያሉት የቃዴስ መሪባ ውኃዎች [ናቸው]።)
am.B: ማኅበሩ በጺን ምድረ በዳ በተጣላ ጊዜ፣ በውኃው አጠገብ በዓይናቸው ፊት ቅድስናዬን እንድትገልጡ የሰጠኋችሁን ትእዛዝ ተላለፋችሁ።» (እነዚህ በጺን ምድረ በዳ በቃዴስ ያሉት የመሪባ ውኃዎች ነበሩ።)
am.R: ይህም የሆነው አንተና አሮን በጺን ምድረ በዳ ትእዛዜን ስለ ተላለፋችሁ ነው። ሕዝቡ በዚያ በተጣላ ጊዜ እኔ ቅዱስ መሆኔን በውኃው አጠገብ አላሳያችኋቸውም።» (ይህ የሆነው በጺን ምድረ በዳ በቃዴስ በሚገኘው በመሪባ ውኃ ነበር።)

decisions.choice: you rebelled: "you" is plural, Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. The LORD speaks to Moses about what he and Aaron did together at Meribah, as in 20:12 and 20:24, where Aaron's death was announced for the same reason.

decisions.choice: rebelled against my command to treat me as holy: the failure at the waters of Meribah
decisions.reason: In 20:1-13 the LORD told Moses to speak to the rock before the people's eyes, but Moses struck it twice and spoke as if he and Aaron were bringing out the water. The LORD said they had not trusted him or shown his holiness before the people (20:12). The command they went against was the command that would have shown the LORD as holy. "Mouth" here means the spoken command.

decisions.choice: Meribah of Kadesh: "quarreling" at Kadesh
decisions.reason: Meribah means "quarreling" and is the same word used just before for the congregation's quarrel. Kadesh comes from the root for "holy", the word in "treat me as holy", so the place names echo what happened there (20:13). The name Meribah was also given to a place near Rephidim (Exodus 17:7), so "of Kadesh" marks which one is meant.

decisions.choice: These are the waters of Meribah: a note to the reader
decisions.reason: The last sentence explains the place named. It reads like the narrator's note, as at 20:13, and is set apart here. It can also be read as the end of the LORD's words, which would not change the meaning.

decisions.choice: command
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "command" for "mouth", which here means what the LORD said. Literal keeps "mouth".

decisions.choice: you and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names Aaron because English "you" does not show the plural, following meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: "너희" for the plural "you", Moses and Aaron; Readable names them ("너와 아론")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is plural (meaning decision); Korean marks the plural with "너희", and Readable says who is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans: God speaks of himself with the plain "나", "내"
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting the English marks on "my" and "me" has nothing to change; respect for God is carried by the honorific -시- in the narrative, as the Korean style guide sets. Recorded once for Numbers 27-33.

decisions.choice: "các ngươi" (L) / "các con" (B) / "con và A-rôn ... các con" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, Moses and Aaron together, and Vietnamese marks the plural in the pronoun.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew infinitive names what they failed to do; a bare "để" would read as their purpose in rebelling.

decisions.choice: vocês se rebelaram (L, B); tu e Arão desobedeceram (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, Moses and Aaron (m1), so Portuguese says "vocês", which shows it as English cannot; Readable names Aaron too, as the English Readable does. "Meribá" and "Zim" are the forms of Exodus 17:7 and Numbers 13:21.

decisions.choice: plural verbs "ዐምፃችኋል", "ተላለፋችሁ" (you, Moses and Aaron); Literal brackets "[ከመቀደስ ይልቅ]" (instead of treating as holy)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you rebelled" is plural, and the Amharic plural verb carries that without naming Aaron at Literal and Balanced. Word for word, "እኔን ለመቀደስ" would mean they rebelled in order to treat God as holy; the bracket gives the sense the Hebrew infinitive has here, the failure to do so.

decisions.choice: the God of the spirits of all flesh: the God who gives every human being life
decisions.reason: The title was first used by Moses and Aaron in 16:22. "Flesh" means living humankind and "spirit" the breath of life God gives (Genesis 2:7; 6:17). Because God gives each person life and knows each one, he can choose the right leader.

decisions.choice: appoint: put someone in charge over others
decisions.reason: The verb has a wide range: to count and muster, as in the census (1:3; 26:2), or to put someone in charge, as here and in 3:10. With "over" it means to set a man in authority over the people.

decisions.choice: let the LORD appoint: a request, not a command
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses a wish addressed respectfully to the LORD in the third person, a polite form of prayer.

decisions.choice: all humankind
decisions.reason: As in 16:22, Balanced says "all humankind" for "all flesh", and Readable turns the title into a statement of what it means.

decisions.choice: roho za wote wenye mwili
decisions.reason: "Mwili wote" would mean "the whole body"; "wote wenye mwili", "all who have flesh", keeps the Hebrew picture while meaning all living humankind, which Balanced says plainly ("wanadamu wote").

decisions.choice: "모든 육체의 영들의 하나님" (Literal); "모든 사람에게 영을 주시는 하나님" (Balanced); "모든 사람에게 생명과 숨을 주시는 하나님" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The title means the God who gives every human being life (meaning decision); Literal keeps "육체" for "flesh", Balanced and Readable say whom it means. The request is put as a polite prayer, not a command (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "Lạy CHÚA ... xin Ngài"
decisions.reason: Readable turns the third-person wish into direct prayer, the usual way Vietnamese addresses God.

decisions.choice: Que ... designe (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb is a wish put respectfully to the LORD in the third person (m3); Portuguese has the same form in "Que ... designe", so Moses' prayer keeps the third person rather than turning to "tu". Balanced says "toda a humanidade" for "all flesh", as the English does.

decisions.choice: go out and come in: lead the people in all their life, especially in war

decisions.choice: like sheep that have no shepherd: a people with no one to guide and protect them
decisions.reason: A shepherd led his flock to food and water and kept it from harm. Leaders were often pictured as shepherds, and a people without a ruler as scattered sheep (1 Kings 22:17; Ezekiel 34:5).

decisions.choice: with no shepherd to care for them

decisions.choice: a man in whom is spirit: a man given the spirit to lead
alternatives: a man in whom is the Spirit (of God)
a man with the spirit of wisdom and courage
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "spirit" with no article and no "of God". It may mean the LORD's Spirit, which rested on the elders in 11:17, 25-29 and was seen in Joseph (Genesis 41:38). It may instead mean the gifts of mind and courage a leader needs; Deuteronomy 34:9 calls Joshua "full of the spirit of wisdom". Either way Joshua is already fit for the task before hands are laid on him.

decisions.choice: lay your hand on him: a sign that he is set apart for his task
decisions.reason: Laying a hand on someone or something marked it out and joined it to the one acting, in offerings (Leviticus 1:4) and in setting the Levites apart (8:10). Here it shows that Joshua is chosen and gives him a share in Moses' authority (verse 20; Deuteronomy 34:9). Verse 23 says Moses laid both hands on him.

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Nun: Moses' assistant
decisions.reason: Joshua had served Moses from his youth (11:28), led Israel in battle (Exodus 17:9-13), and was one of the two spies who trusted the LORD (14:6-9, 30).

decisions.choice: Take Joshua / the spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "for yourself", which in Hebrew goes naturally with "take" and adds nothing in English. They write "the spirit" with a small letter, which keeps both readings of meaning decision m1 open.

decisions.choice: "영" for "spirit", without "성령" or "하나님의 영"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision (footnoted) leaves open whether this is the LORD's Spirit or the gift of wisdom to lead; the bare "영" keeps that open, as the English "the spirit" does.

decisions.choice: "thần linh" (lowercase)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "spirit" with no article, and the English keeps "the spirit" in lowercase; Vietnamese keeps the lowercase word and lets the footnote on the meaning decision speak to it.

decisions.choice: espírito, lowercase; põe a tua mão (L, R), impõe a tua mão (B)
decisions.reason: For Joshua's commissioning (verses 18-23). The Hebrew says only "spirit" (m1), so Portuguese writes "espírito" with a small letter, as the English does, keeping both readings; "o Espírito" would decide for one. Laying a hand on him is the sign that he is set apart (m2): Balanced says "impor a mão", the Portuguese verb for this act, and Literal and Readable the plain "pôr".

decisions.choice: commission: give him his charge as leader
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for "command". Said of a person, it means to give him his orders and appoint him to a task. Deuteronomy 3:28 and 31:7-8, 23 give the words of this charge to Joshua: be strong and courageous, for he will bring Israel into the land.

decisions.choice: before their eyes: in public, so that all would know he was the leader
decisions.reason: The appointment is made before the priest and the whole congregation, so that no one could later question Joshua's right to lead, as Korah questioned Moses (16:3).

decisions.reason: Readable says what commissioning is in plainer words.

decisions.choice: le darás órdenes (L); encomiéndale su cargo (B); dale su encargo (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word for "command"; Literal keeps the giving of orders, Balanced and Readable say what they amount to, a charge as leader. The same wording is used in verse 23.

decisions.choice: tu lui donneras tes ordres (L); confie-lui sa charge (B); donne-lui sa mission (R)

decisions.choice: utamwagiza (L); umkabidhi jukumu lake (B); mpe jukumu lake (R)

decisions.choice: lhe darás ordens (L); confia-lhe a sua missão (B); entrega a ele a sua missão (R)

decisions.choice: majesty: the honor and authority of a leader
decisions.reason: The word means splendor or majesty, often the dignity of a king (Psalm 21:6; 1 Chronicles 29:25). Here it is the standing and authority Moses had among the people, which Joshua is to share.

decisions.choice: some of your majesty: a share, not all of it
decisions.reason: The word "from" marks a part. Joshua receives a share of Moses' authority, enough for the people to follow him, while Moses' place as the one the LORD spoke with face to face stays his own (12:6-8; Deuteronomy 34:10).

decisions.choice: listen: heed and obey
decisions.reason: The verb "hear" often means to listen and do what is said. The people are to follow Joshua as they followed Moses (Deuteronomy 34:9; Joshua 1:16-17).

decisions.choice: authority / obey him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "authority" for the word Literal gives as "majesty", and "obey him" for "listen", the sense in this verse.

decisions.choice: "위엄" (Literal), "권위" (Balanced, Readable) for "majesty"
decisions.reason: The word is the honor and authority of a leader, and Moses gives a share of it (meaning decisions); Literal keeps "위엄", Balanced and Readable name the authority to be obeyed.

decisions.choice: da tua majestade (L); parte da tua autoridade (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "majestade" and the partitive "da" ("some of", m2); Balanced and Readable say "autoridade" and "parte", and "obedecer" for "listen" (m3), as the English does.

source.text: וְלִפְנֵ֨י אֶלְעָזָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ יַעֲמֹ֔ד וְשָׁ֥אַל ל֛וֹ בְּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הָאוּרִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה עַל־פִּ֨יו יֵצְא֜וּ וְעַל־פִּ֣יו יָבֹ֗אוּ ה֛וּא וְכָל־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אִתּ֖וֹ וְכָל־הָעֵדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And before Eleazar the priest he shall stand, and he shall inquire for him by [the] judgment of the Urim before Yahweh; at his mouth they shall go out and at his mouth they shall come in, he and all [the] sons of Israel with him, and all the congregation.

en.L: And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and he shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. At his mouth they shall go out and at his mouth they shall come in, he and all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel with him, and all the congregation."
en.B: He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek decisions for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by means of the Urim. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in, Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} with him, the whole congregation."
en.R: Joshua must go to Eleazar the priest when he needs to know what to do. Eleazar will use the Urim to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided. At the word given through Eleazar, Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, the whole community, will set out and will come back."

es.L: Y delante de Eleazar el sacerdote se presentará, y él consultará por él por el juicio del urim delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Por su boca saldrán y por su boca entrarán, él y todos los hijos de Israel con él, y toda la comunidad».
es.B: Se presentará ante el sacerdote Eleazar, quien buscará para él decisiones delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} por medio del urim. A su palabra saldrán y a su palabra entrarán, Josué y todos los israelitas con él, toda la comunidad».
es.R: Josué tendrá que ir al sacerdote Eleazar cuando necesite saber qué hacer. Eleazar usará el urim para preguntar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} qué es lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha decidido. Según la palabra dada por medio de Eleazar, Josué y todos los israelitas, toda la comunidad, saldrán y volverán».

fr.L: Et il se tiendra devant Éléazar le prêtre, et celui-ci consultera pour lui par le jugement des ourim devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Selon sa bouche ils sortiront et selon sa bouche ils entreront, lui et tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël avec lui, et toute la communauté. »
fr.B: Il se présentera devant le prêtre Éléazar, qui demandera pour lui des décisions devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au moyen des ourim. Sur sa parole ils sortiront, et sur sa parole ils rentreront, Josué et tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} avec lui, toute la communauté. »
fr.R: Josué devra aller trouver le prêtre Éléazar quand il aura besoin de savoir quoi faire. Éléazar se servira des ourim pour demander {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a décidé. C’est sur la parole donnée par Éléazar que Josué et tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, toute la communauté, partiront et reviendront. »

sw.L: Naye atasimama mbele ya Eleazari kuhani, naye atamwulizia shauri kwa hukumu ya Urimu mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kwa kinywa chake watatoka na kwa kinywa chake wataingia, yeye na wana wote wa Israeli pamoja naye, na jumuiya yote."
sw.B: Atasimama mbele ya Eleazari kuhani, ambaye atamtafutia maamuzi mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa njia ya Urimu. Kwa neno lake watatoka, na kwa neno lake wataingia, Yoshua na Waisraeli wote pamoja naye, jumuiya yote."
sw.R: Lazima Yoshua aende kwa Eleazari kuhani anapohitaji kujua la kufanya. Eleazari atatumia Urimu kumwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kile ambacho {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ameamua. Kwa neno litakalotolewa kupitia Eleazari, Yoshua na Waisraeli wote, jumuiya yote, wataondoka na kurudi."

vi.L: Và người sẽ đứng trước thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa, và ông sẽ cầu hỏi cho người bằng sự phán xét của U-rim trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Theo miệng ông họ sẽ đi ra và theo miệng ông họ sẽ đi vào, người và cả con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên với người, và cả hội chúng."
vi.B: Người ấy phải đứng trước thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa, và Ê-lê-a-sa sẽ dùng U-rim để cầu hỏi ý {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho người ấy. Theo lời ông, họ sẽ ra đi, và theo lời ông, họ sẽ trở về, cả Giô-suê lẫn toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên với người, tức là cả hội chúng."
vi.R: Khi cần biết phải làm gì, Giô-suê phải đến gặp thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa. Ê-lê-a-sa sẽ dùng U-rim để hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã quyết định thế nào. Theo lời truyền qua Ê-lê-a-sa, Giô-suê và toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, tức là cả cộng đồng, sẽ lên đường và sẽ trở về."

ko.L: 그리고 그는 제사장 엘르아살 앞에 설 것이고, 엘르아살은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 우림의 판결로 그를 위하여 물을 것이다. 그의 입에 따라 그들이 나가고, 그의 입에 따라 그들이 들어올 것이다. 그와 그와 함께한 이스라엘 자손 모두, 곧 온 회중이 [그러할 것이다]."
ko.B: 여호수아는 제사장 엘르아살 앞에 서야 하고, 엘르아살은 우림으로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그를 위하여 판결을 구할 것이다. 여호수아와 그와 함께한 이스라엘 백성 모두, 곧 온 회중은 엘르아살의 말에 따라 나가고, 그의 말에 따라 들어올 것이다."
ko.R: 여호수아는 무엇을 해야 할지 알아야 할 때마다 제사장 엘르아살에게 가야 한다. 엘르아살은 우림을 써서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 무엇을 정하셨는지 여쭈어 볼 것이다. 엘르아살을 통해 주어진 말씀에 따라 여호수아와 이스라엘 사람들 모두, 곧 온 회중이 길을 떠나고 돌아올 것이다."

pt.L: E diante de Eleazar, o sacerdote, ele estará, e [Eleazar] consultará por ele o juízo do Urim diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; pela sua boca sairão e pela sua boca entrarão, ele e todos os filhos de Israel com ele, e toda a comunidade."
pt.B: Ele se apresentará ao sacerdote Eleazar, que buscará para ele as decisões {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} por meio do Urim. Pela palavra de Eleazar eles sairão e pela palavra dele voltarão, Josué e todos os israelitas com ele, toda a comunidade."
pt.R: Josué deve ir ao sacerdote Eleazar quando precisar saber o que fazer. Eleazar vai usar o Urim para perguntar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} decidiu. De acordo com a palavra dada por meio de Eleazar, Josué e todos os israelitas, toda a comunidade, vão partir e vão voltar."

am.L: በካህኑም በአልዓዛር ፊት ይቆማል፤ እርሱም በኡሪም ፍርድ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ይጠይቅለታል። እርሱና ከእርሱ ጋር ያሉት የእስራኤል ልጆች ሁሉ፣ ማኅበሩም ሁሉ በአፉ ይወጣሉ፣ በአፉም ይገባሉ።»
am.B: እርሱ በካህኑ በአልዓዛር ፊት ይቁም፤ አልዓዛርም በኡሪም አማካይነት {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ውሳኔ ይጠይቅለታል። ኢያሱና ከእርሱ ጋር ያሉት የእስራኤል ልጆች ሁሉ፣ ማኅበሩ በሙሉ፣ በእርሱ ቃል ይወጣሉ፤ በእርሱም ቃል ይገባሉ።»
am.R: ኢያሱ ምን ማድረግ እንዳለበት ማወቅ ሲፈልግ ወደ ካህኑ ወደ አልዓዛር መሄድ አለበት። አልዓዛርም በኡሪም አማካይነት {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ምን እንደ ወሰነ ይጠይቃል። ኢያሱና እስራኤላውያን ሁሉ፣ ማኅበሩ በሙሉ፣ በአልዓዛር በኩል በተሰጠው ቃል ይነሣሉ፤ ይመለሳሉም።»

decisions.choice: before Eleazar he shall stand: Joshua will seek the LORD's will through the priest
decisions.reason: Moses spoke with the LORD face to face (12:8; Exodus 33:11). Joshua will not; he will learn the LORD's will through the high priest. Leadership after Moses is shared between the leader and the priest.

decisions.choice: the judgment of the Urim: a decision sought from the LORD with the sacred lots
decisions.reason: The Urim, with the Thummim, were kept in the high priest's breastpiece and used to ask the LORD for a decision (Exodus 28:30; 1 Samuel 28:6). Only the Urim is named here, standing for both. How they were used is not told; they probably gave a yes or no answer. The name is left untranslated, as in Exodus 28:30.

decisions.choice: at his mouth: at the word Eleazar gives from the LORD
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to Eleazar, who gives the answer from the LORD; the next words make Joshua and the people the ones who go out at that word. It could also refer to the LORD, whose decision Eleazar seeks. In either case the people move at the LORD's word given through the priest.

decisions.choice: go out and come in: set out on campaigns and journeys and return
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the pair covers all the people's ventures, especially going out to war.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joshua where the Hebrew says "he", since the sentence has already spoken of Eleazar and "he" could be misread. Readable also says "at the word given through Eleazar", which fits both readings of meaning decision m3, and adds "when he needs to know what to do" to say why Joshua stands before the priest.

decisions.choice: "우림의 판결" (Literal), "우림으로 판결을 구하다" (Balanced), "우림을 써서 여쭈어 보다" (Readable)
decisions.reason: "우림" is the term sheet form; the phrase is a decision sought from the LORD with the sacred lots (meaning decision). Readable describes what Eleazar does.

decisions.choice: "여호수아" and "엘르아살" named at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Korean leaves the pronouns unclear in a sentence with two men; the names make plain that Joshua stands before Eleazar and that "his word" is the word Eleazar gives (meaning decision, footnoted).

decisions.choice: "người" for Joshua and "ông" for Eleazar at L; the names at B and R
decisions.reason: Vietnamese third-person pronouns would make the two men hard to tell apart; Literal gives each its own pronoun, and Balanced and Readable name them, as the English does.

decisions.choice: [Eleazar] (L); Pela palavra de Eleazar (B)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "ele" and "dele" would most readily point to Joshua, the subject of the sentence. Literal names Eleazar in brackets as the one who inquires, and Balanced names him at "his mouth", the reading m3 prefers, as the English Readable does; Balanced names Joshua as the English does. "O Urim" is the name Exodus 28:30 uses.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֨הוּ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָּל־הָעֵדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And did Moses as commanded Yahweh him; and he took Joshua and made stand him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation,

en.L: And Moses did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, and he took Joshua and made him stand before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation,
en.B: Moses did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation,
en.R: Moses did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told him. He brought Joshua and had him stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the whole community.

es.L: E hizo Moisés como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado; y tomó a Josué y lo hizo estar delante de Eleazar el sacerdote y delante de toda la comunidad,
es.B: Moisés hizo como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había ordenado. Tomó a Josué y lo hizo presentarse ante el sacerdote Eleazar y toda la comunidad,
es.R: Moisés hizo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo. Llevó a Josué y lo puso delante del sacerdote Eleazar y de toda la comunidad.

fr.L: Et Moïse fit comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui avait ordonné ; il prit Josué et le fit se tenir devant Éléazar le prêtre et devant toute la communauté,
fr.B: Moïse fit ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait ordonné. Il prit Josué et le fit se présenter devant le prêtre Éléazar et toute la communauté,
fr.R: Moïse a fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait dit. Il a amené Josué et l’a fait se tenir devant le prêtre Éléazar et toute la communauté.

sw.L: Naye Musa akafanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru; akamchukua Yoshua, akamsimamisha mbele ya Eleazari kuhani na mbele ya jumuiya yote,
sw.B: Musa alifanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru. Alimchukua Yoshua, akamsimamisha mbele ya Eleazari kuhani na jumuiya yote,
sw.R: Musa alifanya kile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alichomwambia. Alimleta Yoshua, akamsimamisha mbele ya Eleazari kuhani na jumuiya yote.

vi.L: Và Môi-se làm y như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho ông; ông đem Giô-suê và cho người đứng trước thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và trước cả hội chúng,
vi.B: Môi-se làm đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho ông. Ông đem Giô-suê đến, cho người ấy đứng trước thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và cả hội chúng,
vi.R: Môi-se làm theo lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán dặn. Ông đem Giô-suê đến và cho người ấy đứng trước mặt thầy tế lễ Ê-lê-a-sa và cả cộng đồng.

ko.L: 그리고 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 명령하신 대로 하였다. 그는 여호수아를 데려다가 제사장 엘르아살 앞과 온 회중 앞에 세우고,
ko.B: 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 명령하신 대로 했다. 그는 여호수아를 데려다가 제사장 엘르아살과 온 회중 앞에 세우고,
ko.R: 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 대로 했다. 그는 여호수아를 데려와서 제사장 엘르아살과 온 회중 앞에 세웠다.

pt.L: E Moisés fez como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe ordenara; e tomou Josué e o fez estar de pé diante de Eleazar, o sacerdote, e diante de toda a comunidade,
pt.B: Moisés fez como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe tinha ordenado. Ele tomou Josué e o fez ficar diante do sacerdote Eleazar e de toda a comunidade,
pt.R: Moisés fez o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe mandou. Ele levou Josué e o fez ficar de pé diante do sacerdote Eleazar e de toda a comunidade.

am.L: ሙሴም {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዳዘዘው አደረገ፤ ኢያሱንም ወስዶ በካህኑ በአልዓዛርና በማኅበሩ ሁሉ ፊት አቆመው፤
am.B: ሙሴ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዳዘዘው አደረገ። ኢያሱን ወስዶ በካህኑ በአልዓዛርና በማኅበሩ ሁሉ ፊት አቆመው፤
am.R: ሙሴ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የነገረውን አደረገ። ኢያሱን አምጥቶ በካህኑ በአልዓዛርና በማኅበሩ ሁሉ ፊት አቆመው።

decisions.choice: Moses did as the LORD commanded: his last act of leadership in Numbers is obedience
decisions.reason: Moses had been told that he went against the LORD's command at Meribah (verse 14). Here he does exactly what he is told, in front of all the people.

source.text: וַיִּסְמֹ֧ךְ אֶת־יָדָ֛יו עָלָ֖יו וַיְצַוֵּ֑הוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as had spoken Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken by the hand of Moses.
en.B: and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had directed through Moses.
en.R: Then Moses laid his hands on Joshua and gave him his charge, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Moses.

decisions.choice: his hands: both hands, where verse 18 says "hand"
decisions.reason: The LORD told Moses to lay his hand on Joshua (verse 18), and Moses lays both hands on him. The singular in verse 18 names the act, and the meaning is the same. Deuteronomy 34:9 also says "his hands".

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" someone means through that person as the LORD's agent. It is the usual way Numbers speaks of the LORD's commands given through Moses (4:37; 9:23; 15:23).

decisions.choice: through Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "by the hand of"; Literal keeps the picture. Readable names Moses and Joshua for clarity.

decisions.choice: "hai tay"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plural "hands" here where verse 18 has "hand"; Vietnamese marks it with "hai".

decisions.choice: pela mão de Moisés (L); por meio de Moisés (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the book sets at 4:37: Literal keeps the idiom "by the hand of" (m2), and Balanced and Readable say "por meio de". "As suas mãos" is plural here, where verse 18 says "a tua mão" (m1).
